mathematical_findings: P24.5 now explicitly restricts to nonempty retained words k>=1; conditioning gives exactly the positive prior-support fibre, and q is identifiable iff constant on that fibre.

Known bijective dynamics carries initial and current compatible-state sets bijectively; product readout fixes the current visible coordinate, so current hidden identification iff the same fibre is singleton. Neither point survives arbitrary missing current readout or noninjective dynamics.

The partition refinement proof uses whole carrier size N, with max(1,N-1) observations. It does not substitute noninvariant support size. Consecutive partition equality gives forward stability; otherwise class count strictly increases until discrete.

Universal ambiguity is correctly equivalent to all NONEMPTY intersections of full future-trace classes with the admissible support having at least two members. Proper instantaneous readout is insufficient.
C4 predictive-memory and capacity claims do not lower-bound residual hidden entropy conditioned on the whole retained history. The swap has one bit of readback and zero residual hidden entropy.

For the cyclic (m+1)-bit register, full conditional past/future information at t=m is m bits, whereas the next-step conditional information is one bit. Both coexist with zero residual current-hidden entropy after m+1 readings.

R stored values for |A|>R force some fibre of size at least ceil(|A|/R), not every fibre to be non-singleton. Physical record retention, model/prior knowledge, interventions, physical branch selection, coherent instrument theory and the full gauge relation remain additional hypotheses or open problems.
Known-model record-fibre state inference remains distinct from P24.4 unknown-model predictive-quotient reconstruction, which retains its own full-support and state-bound assumptions.
